name: CA-39
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 7 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Mark Takano is running with a large fundraising edge

model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Takano: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a clear money advantage, with markets agreeing at roughly 97%. With no polls or ratings to contradict that, the race stays at Safe D.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race, or a surge of outside spending for Manos, would be the signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Mark Takano, the Democratic incumbent, is favored to win another term in this Riverside-area House district. The seat leans Democratic by about seven points, and the national environment this cycle adds to that edge. Takano has raised roughly $894,000 and holds a cash advantage, while Republican Steve Manos reports little fundraising and draws no outside support. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97%. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the forecast rests on fundamentals. The race is rated Safe D, with Takano expected to win by roughly 20 points, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of direct polling.
